$comment: Registrable domains treated as known-safe by the `allowlist` check.
A hit here short-circuits the verdict to `safe` AND suppresses the Layer-2 network call
(golden rule 2: an allowlisted host must never be sent anywhere). That makes this file a
security-sensitive list — anything here is un-flaggable, so a compromised entry is a blind
1. Match on the REGISTRABLE DOMAIN only, never a substring. 'google.com.evil.ru' must not
match 'google.com'. parse.js computes eTLD+1 and the check compares it exactly.
2. Keep it to domains whose compromise would be front-page news. This is not a directory of
good websites; it is a list of domains where a false 'danger' would destroy trust.
example.com is deliberately ABSENT. It is the brand used throughout the test fixtures and the
smoke page, and allowlisting it would silence every fixture built on it.
The user's own allowlist (chrome.storage.sync) is merged in at call time by the content
script — it is not stored here.
